key_idea: The number of (B at i, A at i+k) pairs for every k is a cross-correlation of the two indicator arrays, i.e. one convolution after reversing one of them.
sketch: Let A[i]=1 where s[i]='A' and R[n-1-i]=1 where s[i]='B'; then the product coefficient at n-1+k equals the number of k-inversions. Multiply with an NTT of size 2^21 modulo 998244353; counts are at most 1e6 so there is no wraparound. O(n log n), about 0.2s. Pitfalls: get the reversal offset right and use fast output for up to 1e6 lines.
